molasses.text: Imagine walking down the street... when a giant wave of thick, sticky liquid comes rushing toward you.
On the waterfront stood a fifty-foot steel tank, holding over two million gallons of molasses.
It leaked so badly, it was painted brown to hide the stains.
Then the rivets started popping, like gunfire... and the tank burst apart.
A wave up to twenty-five feet high tore through the streets at around thirty-five miles an hour.
It crushed buildings, and twisted the steel of an elevated railway.
And here's what made it so deadly. In the freezing air, the molasses thickened like glue.
Anyone caught in it couldn't escape.
Sailors, police and Red Cross nurses waded in to help.
Twenty-one people died. About a hundred and fifty were injured.
It sounds unbelievable. But it was real... and it changed building safety rules for good.
